However, the BharatNet implementation track record needs to significantly improve for benefits to reach rural India. Broadband penetration has a direct impact on economic growth, employment, innovation and prosperity. A strong push to transport connectivity, healthcare and education through the digital media are likely to have a significant, long-term impact on the telecom ecosystem.

I wish to add that the proposals of benefits in many social sectors given by the Finance Minister will be helpful for the underprivileged sections and since the income tax rates has been reduced, the tendency of the person of not paying the tax will go down. I also hail this Budget as growth oriented and progressive. The budget continues to focus on important measures initiated by our Government and is focused on both consumption and investment demand. This budget has given focus on rural economy, small and medium enterprises, small income tax payers and importantly bringing reforms in political funding. This is a forward looking budget directed towards raising the productivity in the economy with a focus to transform, energize and clean India. With a keen focus on infrastructure and all round development, the budget – under the leadership of our Hon'ble P.M. – will strengthen economic fundamentals – a focus of the Government since 2014. This budget firmly establishes the winds of change for India ushered in by demonetization and GST.

I want action for bringing unsalaried class with more income into the tax net. I also appreciate the cap of Rs. 3 lakh for cash transactions. To check black-money and promote digital economy, the budget proposes no cash transaction above 3 lakh rupees. The duties on devices used for cashless transactions are reduced.

I endorse the inclusion of Railway budget proposals in General budget as a historic step; the budget has come up with many proposals for extension and development of railway network, besides making a big allocation of one lakh crore rupees for railway safety.

I also support the thrust accorded by the Budget to multi modal transport planning and synergizing investments in railways, roads, waterways and civil aviation. Development of multi-modal transport hubs would help ease traffic congestion to a large extent and also bring down pollution.

This Budget has brought transparency in funding of political parties. Now, donations above Rs. 2000 must be made in cheque/draft. Every political party will have to file its return within the time prescribed in the Income Tax Act.

श्री बोध सिंह भगत (बालाघाट) : माननीय अध्यक्ष जी, मैं माननीय अरुण जेटली जी, वित्त मंत्री द्वारा 2017-18 के प्रस्तुत लोकप्रिय आम बजट पर माननीय प्रधानमंत्री एवं वित्त मंत्री जी के प्रति धन्यवाद प्रे­िषत करता हूं। यह बजट गांव, गरीब और किसानों के जीवन में बेहतरी एवं युवाओं के लिए रोजगार के नए अवसरों का सृजन करने की दिशा में कारगर साबित होगा। साथ ही साथ यह बजट राजकोषीय सुदृढ़ीकरण के प्रति भी प्रतिबद्धता दर्शाता है। इसमें राजकोषीय घाटे के 3.2 प्रतिशत लक्ष्य के अनुरूप रहते हुए संशोधित अनुमान 2016-17 की तुलना में 1,32,328 करोड़ वृद्धि की पु­िष्ट की गई है।

मैं स्वयं एक मेहनतकश सीमांत ग्रामीण किसान हूं एवं गांव, गरीब और किसानों की समस्याओं को भलीभांति समझता हूं। इसलिए यह विश्वास के साथ कह सकता हूं कि यह बजट किसानों की आय को दोगुना करने एवं पंडित दीन दयाल उपाध्याय जी द्वारा दी गयी अन्त्योदय की परिकल्पना, शो­िषत, पीड़ित, वंचित एवं आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग के कल्याण के लिए प्रधान मंत्री जी की प्रतिबद्धता दर्शाता है। साथ ही प्रधान मंत्री जी का मूल मंत्र ‘सबका साथ, सबका विकास’ के प्रति भी यह बजट प्रतिबद्धता दर्शाता है। इस बजट में ग्रामीण विकास के लिए मनरेगा के अंतर्गत वर्ष 2017-18 में 48 हजार करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया था, जो वर्ष 2016-17 के 37,499 की तुलना में काफी अधिक है। प्रधान मंत्री आवास योजना में 29043 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है। स्वास्थ्य के क्षेत्र में वर्ष 2017-2018 में 27,131 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है। स्वच्छ भारत अभियान में 16,248 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है। 

नैशनल मिशन प्रधान मंत्री फसल बीमा योजना के लिए 9 हजार करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है। इन्द्रधनु­ष योजना के तहत बैंकों का पुनः पूंजीकरण करने के लिए 10 हजार करोड़ रुपये एवं रा­ष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण पेयजल योजना हेतु भी 6050 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान रखा गया है। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा मिशन में 29,556 करोड़ रुपये का बजट प्रावधान किया गया है, जो दस परसेंट की वृद्धि दर्शाता है। 

प्रधानमंत्री कृषि सिंचाई योजना में 20 हजार करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान रखा गया है। गरीब परिवार को एल.पी.जी. के लिए ढाई हजार करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान रखा गया है। ढाई लाख से पांच लाख रुपये तक की आय पर दस परसेंट आयकर को कम करके पांच परसेंट कर दिया है, जिससे 1 करोड़ 95 लाख लोगों को लाभ मिलेगा। डिजिटल इंडिया को बढ़ावा देते हुए वर्ष 2017-18 के अंत तक डेढ़ लाख ग्राम पंचायतों तक आप्टिकल फाइबर के जरिए हाई स्पीड ब्राडबैंड कनेक्टिविटी का प्रावधान किया गया है। देश के साढ़े तीन करोड़ युवाओं को प्रशिक्षण के लिए संकल्प योजना के तहत 42 सौ करोड़ रुपये आबंटित किये गये हैं। इसके साथ-साथ 50 हजार ग्राम पंचायतों को गरीबी मुक्त करने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है। ...(व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : भगत जी, अब आप अपनी बात समाप्त कीजिए।

श्री बोध सिंह भगत: अध्यक्ष महोदया, हमें पहली बार संघर्ष करके बोलने का मौका मिला है। ...(व्यवधान) आप हमें दो मिनट और बोलने का मौका दीजिए। ...(व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : ठीक है, आप बोलिये।

श्री बोध सिंह भगत:  अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं रेल मंत्री जी को भी धन्यवाद देना चाहता हू, क्योंकि उन्होंने ब्राडगेज लाइन के विस्तार के लिए 1 हजार 80 करोड़ रुपये दिये हैं। यात्री सुरक्षा, साफ-सफाई तथा खान-पान आदि के लिए पर्याप्त राशि दी गयी है। इससे निश्चित ही यात्रियों को रेल सुविधा प्राप्त होगी।

अध्यक्ष महोदया, मेरा जिला नक्सल प्रभावित जिला है। बालाघाट-सिवनी आदिवासी जिला है, जो काफी पिछड़ा हुआ है। इस जिले में काफी विकास कार्यों की आवश्यकता है। मेरा आपके माध्यम से अनुरोध है कि नक्सल प्रभावित जिलों के लिए कुछ विशे­ष पैकेज दिया जाये। धन्यवाद।

*DR. THOKCHOM MEINYA (INNER MANIPUR): This time, the Union Budget (UB) is presented on the 1st day of February. Reading the budget at 1100 hrs instead of 1700 hrs had been effected to enable maximum number of our population to hear it or to remove the colonial stigma. Whatever may be the reason, change is the order of the day. The names of many schemes/ programmes/streets are being changed. History will maintain the record and we shall always sing the song that ‘Variety is the mother of enjoyment’ and ‘the world is dynamic’. 

Again, another structural change in the present Union Budget is the amalgamation of erstwhile Railway budget into it and now we have only one Union Budget. Next, it could be budget less or less Budget as we are going in the direction of cash less or less cash. I could be really interesting to run the country’s administration/governance without any Budget. What a wonderful idea/ hypothesis!

The Hon. Finance Minister tried to steadying the ship of monetization. We have to see how far he will be successful. The FM’s budget appears to take the position of the left-of-centre space from the Opposition. The proceedings of November 8, 2016, wherein a major finance decision was taken apparently without his knowledge, might have given him this position. In the words of the Government, this Budget stands for sustainable growth. But the question is: Is the negative growth a sustainable growth?

In terms of budget allocation for social sector, Hon FM tried very hard to keep it at status-quo. In this case also, I am afraid; Hon FM is not able to succeed. Yes, there is status-quo allocation of fund in some few major social sector schemes at the cost of majority of many other counterparts.

Now I come to the most critical part of the Budget. When it comes to education, the Budget’s attention deficit continues. This is really shocking. Because in a developing democracy like ours, proper empowering of its people is fundamental which is possible only through education. Still, I do stand by my demand to the Union Government to provide a good school in every Indian village. A good school requires good roads leading to the school, proper water and power supply over and above the required qualified trained teachers and proper physical infrastructure of the school. I hope the Government does understand it! It is only education that can meaningfully empower our citizens. By properly empowering the citizens, democracy will bear fruits.

Union Government’s seeing the North Eastern States as the Ashtalakshmi that can take India to new heights; telling that the North East is the gateway of South East Asia; putting in place infamous Look-East (now Act-East) policy only in name; and continuing with the special dispensation in the assistance pattern to the North-eastern states by providing assistance in the ration of 90:10 for core central schemes and 80:20 for non-core schemes to these states will not serve any purpose until and unless the Union Government practices the principle of mutual co-existence at par with the rest of the country in every respect. This is exactly what is lacking on the part of the Union Government.

Let us take the case of more than 100 days long economic blockade on the two NHs of Manipur called by the United Naga Council (UNC). The Union Government has practically and absolutely failed to open the almost three month long economic blockade called by UNC on the two NHs, Nos. 2 and 37, the only lifelines of Manipur. The economic blockade of National Highways of Manipur has been called by United Naga Council (UNC) since 1st November last year. People of the State are facing insurmountable hardships. The prices of essential commodities including petroleum products have sky-rocketed. Life-saving drugs are in acute shortage. The situation is still no better.

The long-awaited tripartite talk of Union Government, State Government and UNC has been initiated on 3rd February. Day before yesterday, the 7th February, UNC Presidential Council Meeting decided to continue the blockade. At the same time, State Assembly Election notification was issued on the same day. What is this? It appears that every body’s business is nobody’s business. At the end, who suffers – only the common people suffer.

Economic blockade is not the right way. It is but a crime against humanity. It has created hatred among us, let us stop it. I urge upon UNC to immediately call off the economic blockade.

Also, I demand for the establishment of dedicated NHs Protection Security Forces to regulate 24x7 smooth flows of vehicles for passengers and goods on these NHs.

I strongly urge upon the Union Government to immediately intervene and help the State Government to mitigate the situation before it is too late.

Law and order situation in the border states of the country like J&K and the NE India is still a matter of grave concern. In these States, the Armed Forces (Special) Powers Act (AFSPA), 1958 has been promulgated since 80’s, and here Army is engaged in counter-insurgency operations under the Act. This Act provides immunity to the army from being tried without the prior permission of the Union Government. Under this Act, the state of Manipur has seen many orphans, widows, parents who do not know whereabouts of their missing children. Rapes, fake encounters, custodian killings are rampant.

In spite of the recommendations of various committees, conferences, UN bodies to repeal the Act, the Government of India is still shy to repeal this draconian law. However, the Government of Manipur has lifted AFSPA from the seven Assembly Constituencies under Imphal Municipality.

I am always for the immediate repeal of this AFSPA. Time has come for this draconian Act to go. I do very sincerely urge upon the Union Government please repeal this Act immediately for the sack of humanity.

In para 63, the Hon President has stated; I quote “Over eleven hundred obsolete laws have been repealed and 400 more are in the process of being repealed. Legislations relating to Women, Divyang Jan, Labour, Apprentices, Factories, Benami Transactions, Aadhar and Real Estate, to mention a few – mirror my Government’s guiding philosophy of Transparency, and Social Justice.”

Here I would like to request the Union Government, Ministry of Home Affairs in particular, to include in the list, laws relating to the violation of human rights which are also obsolete. One such legislation is the Armed Forces (Special) Powers Act (AFSPA), 1958. This law is a manifestation of the colonial law legislated way back in 1942. I once again urge the Union Government to immediately repeal this draconian law.

With these observations, I strongly oppose the Union Budget 2017-18.

HON. SPEAKER: Shri C.N. Jayadevan, only two minutes not more than that. 

SHRI C.N. JAYADEVAN (THRISSUR): Thank you, Madam, for giving me this opportunity to participate in the discussion on the General Budget, 2017-18 on behalf of my party, the Communist Party of India. 

Initially, as a general view, I must give my opinion that the present Budget has once again put down the hopes of the common man, the vulnerable population like the old, tribals, dalits and women. Moreover the Budget is very much inline with the new liberal outlook of the present Government as there are concessions for the corporate houses at the cost of the middle class community. 

Considering the agricultural sector and the farmer’s community, the loan limit for the farmers have been raised to Rs. 10 lakhs but no measures are in place for solving the increasing suicides of farmers and the drought conditions prevailing in different parts of the country. When there is a boom in the agricultural production, farmers are in doom due to the crash in prices of their produce. 

The alternate employment scheme, the MGNREGA, has been allotted the highest amount, that is Rs. 48,000 crore till date as per the Finance Minister. But he is very well silent on the fact that Rs. 14,000 crore is the backlog from the previous year for the payment of wages.

Basic facilities like health and education are also not given due consideration. The allocation of six per cent of GDP to education, as recommended by Kothari Commission, is till a far dream. There are also highly ambitious targets for eliminating diseases like measles and tuberculosis, etc. But I strongly advise that apart from higher allocations, a mission mode working is required. 

The proposal to increase the medical PG seats at the rate of 5000 post-graduate seats per year does not mention anything about AYUSH system of medicine. In this context, I would request the Minister to allocate a fair percentage of these 5000 seats to the AYUSH system of medicine also, particularly Ayurveda which has a great potential for earning foreign exchange also. 

Overall, the Union Budget reflects a casual approach that the present Government has taken on the crisis-ridden economy of the country. Even the Chief Economic Advisor is of the opinion that assessment of demonetisation can be termed as a ‘carpet bomb’. I repeat, your demonetisation and your Budget is a carpet bomb. It can only be met after years. By that time, the time of the present Government would end.

Thank you, Madam.

डॉ. बंशीलाल महतो (कोरबा) : मैडम, मैं कोरबा, छत्तीसगढ़ से आता हूं। जिस प्रकार से हम भारत को भारत माता के नाम से जानते हैं, उसी प्रकार छत्तीसगढ़ को हम लोग " छत्तीसगढ़ महतारी " के नाम से जानते हैं। किसी प्रदेश के नाम के साथ महतारी शब्द नहीं जुड़ा है। छत्तीसगढ़ में माता कौशल्या का जन्म हुआ था और भगवान राम हमारे भानजे हैं। 

मैडम, मैं इस बजट का समर्थन करने के लिए खड़ा हुआ हूं। यह बजट अत्यंत लाभदायक, सर्वस्पर्शी, सर्वव्यापी, सर्वसुलभ और सभी को ध्यान में रखने वाला बजट है। तुलसी कृत रामायण की एक चौपाई है:

‘मुखिया मुख सो चाहिए, खान-पान को एक।

पालहि, पोसहि सकल जगत, तुलसी सहित विवेक।’

यह बहुत अच्छी चौपाई है और इसी के अनुसार हमारे देश के प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्रभाई मोदी और वित्त मंत्री जी ने इस बजट को बनाया है, जो आम जनता, किसान, गरीब, युवा और महिलाओं के लिए अत्यंत ही लाभदायी है। सभी चीजों में पहले की अपेक्षा बजट एलोकेशन ज्यादा हुआ है। 

मैं एक बात कहना चाहता हूं, जैसा अभी मेरे पूर्व वक्ता कह रहे थे, आयु­ष का बजट पहले की अपेक्षा कम कर दिया गया है, जबकि यह पार्टी भारतीय संस्कृति की पो­ाक पार्टी है। हमारी सरकार भारतीय संस्कृति को बढ़ावा देने वाली सरकार है, शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में हो या स्वास्थ्य के क्षेत्र में हो। आयु­ष का बजट गत वर्ष कम था, मैंने बोला भी था, उस समय बजट 1391 करोड़ रुपये थे। इस साल उसका बजट मात्र 441 करोड़ रुपये है, जो इनसफिशिएंट है। एक मेडिकल कॉलेज की स्थापना में कम से कम 700 से 800 करोड़ रुपये खर्च होते हैं। पूरे देश के लिए आयु­ष के लिए 441 करोड़ रुपये का बजट अत्यंत ही कम है। भारतीय चिकित्सा पद्धति में एक चिकित्सा, जिसे हम पंचकर्म कहते हैं, विश्व की अद्वितीय चिकित्सा पद्धति है। पंचकर्म से कायकल्प होता है। इसलिए इसके बजट को बढ़ाया जाना चाहिए। जितने आंकड़े सभी लोगों ने पेश किए हैं, उनसे मैं सहमत हूं। आंकड़े बहुत हैं और हम लोगों ने जिस प्रकार से विचार करके यह अच्छा बजट बनाया है, वह सराहनीय है। 

पहले पासपोर्ट बनाने में बहुत कठिनाई होती थी, इस बजट में इस बात का ध्यान रखा गया है कि अब पासपोर्ट बड़े डाकघरों से भी मिलेंगे। इसी प्रकार से कोयला खदान में काम करने वाले लोग हैं या माइन्स-मिनरल्स के जितने पैसे हैं, खनिज न्यास हैं, उनको पहली बार सरकार ने उसी एरिया में खर्च करने का प्रावधान किया है। मोदी सरकार की यह बहुत बड़ी देन है। 

मैं कोरबा जिले से आता हूं, वहां तीन वर्ष के लिए 635 करोड़ रुपये खर्च होंगे। उसका एलोकेशन हमें प्राप्त हो चुका है। हम सभी लोगों ने नदी-नालों को बांधने में, स्टॉप डैम बनाने में उसको खर्च किया है। एक-एक बूंद पानी बचाने की बात है, एक-एक बूंद पानी पहुंचाने की बात है। तुलसीदास जी ने उत्तरकाण्ड में लिखा है - कागभुशुण्डि जी ने गरूड़ जी से कहा कि कलयुग में बार-बार अकाल पड़ेगा, जहां-जहां पानी की व्यवस्था होगी, वहीं-वहीं फसल होगी। उस बात को ध्यान में रखते हुए मोदी जी ने प्रधानमंत्री सिंचाई योजना लागू की है, ताकि अधिक से अधिक फसल का उत्पादन हो और इस देश में अकाल न पड़े। अगर अकाल पड़े, तब भी पानी की व्यवस्था रहे, जिससे फसल का उत्पादन हो सके। इस बात पर हम लोगों ने ध्यान दिया है। छत्तीसगढ़ का सबसे बड़ा बांध मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र में है -हसदेव बंगो बांध। भारतवर्ष में सबसे ज्यादा नेशनल हाईवेज कोरबा संसदीय क्षेत्र में है। इस प्रकार से कोरबा क्षेत्र भाग्यशाली है, धनवान क्षेत्र है, लेकिन वहां पर कुछ और ज्यादा सरकारी मद मिले तो ज्यादा विकास होगा। धन्यवाद।

*श्री भानु प्रताप सिंह वर्मा (जालौन)ः जिस दौर में राजनीति वायदों और चमकदार घोषणाओं से की जाती हो, उस दौर में राजनीति से दूर और सबका साथ सबका विकास जसे विचार से ओत प्रोत इस धर्मनिरपेक्ष बजट के लिये मैं माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मादी, माननीय वित्त मंत्री श्री अरूण जेटली, माननीय वित्त राज्य मंत्री श्री अर्जुनराम मेघवाल जी एवं संतोष गंगवार जी को धन्यवाद देता हूँ और माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी को बधाई देता हूँ कि आजाद भारत के पहले संयुक्त बजट को पेश करने के लिये जैसे व्यक्तित्व की आवश्यकता थी उन्होंने वैसा ही परिचय दिया।

महात्मा गांधी जी का मानना था कि बिना गांवों के विकास के इस देश का विकास संभव नहीं और इस बजट में ग्रामीण विकास के लिये तीन लाख करोड़ के रिकॉर्ड बजट की धोषणा करके हमने यह स्पष्ट कर दिया कि हम गांधी जी के सपनों के भारत के निर्माण की दिशा में अग्रसर है। इसके अतिरिक्त 2019 तक हर गांव में बिजली, 2022 तक किसानों की आय दुगनी करने के हमारे संकल्प बताते हैं कि माननीय प्रधानमंत्री के नेतृत्व वाली एनडीए सरकार इस देश की सबसे दृढ़ संकल्पों वाली सरकार है। कैशलैस इकॉनमी के लिये हमारे दृढ़ संकल्प, नोटबंदी जैसे साहसिक कदम लेकर जनधन खातों को डॉयरेक्ट बेनिफट ट्रांसफर से जोड़कर हम अर्थव्यवस्था के क्षेत्र से पूरी तरह से भ्रष्टाचार खत्म कर देंगे।

यूपीए वाले कह रहे हैं कि उनके समय के बजट अच्छे होते थे, उन्होंने तमाम अन्तर गिनाये मैं भी एक अन्तर गिनाता हूं पहले इनकी सरकार में जब बजट आता था तो जनता में चर्चाएं होती थी फलां विभाग को इतना बजट हैं अब इसमें घोटाला होगा, फलां को इतना है, अब इसमें भी घोटाला होगा। इस क्षेत्र में इतना घोटाला हुआ है उस क्षेत्र में इतना घोटाला हुआ है, अब चर्चा होती है कि इस क्षेत्र को विकास के लिये इतना पैसा है इसके लिये इतना है सड़क परिवहन में इतना तेजी से काम हो रहा है रेल में और तेजी से काम हो रहा है। पहले मंत्रालयों में भ्रष्टाचार पर प्रतयोगिता होती थी अब प्रगति पर प्रतियोगिता होती है, मनरेगा में महिलाओं की हिस्सेदारी बढ़ाकर 55 प्रतिशत कर दी गई है जो हमारी मातृशक्ति को हमारा सम्मान है। अब ग्रामीण क्षेत्र की महिलायें भी ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था की भागीदार बनेंगी। 

पिछले दिनों 20 नवम्बर, 2016 को मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत पुखराया स्टेशन के निकट जो दुखद हादसा हुआ था उस की जांच में एनआईए की कुछ और टीमें बढ़ा देनी चाहिए, ताकि आईएसआई जैसी आंतकी संस्थाओं के खतरनाक मंसूबों पर पानी फेरा जा सके। इसके अतिरिक्त मैं मांग करना चाहूंगा कि पिछले वर्ष रेल बजट में घोषित कोंच भिण्ड लाइन तथा उरई महोबा के निर्माण की दिशा में राज्य सरकारों से वार्ता कर उन्हें जल्द से जल्द बनाया जाये तथा कोंच से जालौन होते हुए फफूंद रेल लाइन का निर्माण भी कराया जाये। इसके अतिरिक्त मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में स्थानीय सड़कों की जो स्थिति है उसे ध्यान में रखते हुए केन्द्रीय सड़क निधि द्वारा उखड़ चुकी सड़को का पुनः निर्माण कराया जाये।

मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र से आने जाने हेतु कोई भी एक ट्रेन नहीं है। दिल्ली से कानपुर जाने वाली श्रमशक्ति एक्सप्रेस जो कानपुर में करीब 18(अठारह) घंटे खड़ी रहती है यदि श्रम शक्ति को कानपुर से झांसी तक बढ़ा दिया जाए तो निश्चित रेलवे की आय बढ़ेगी तथा, एटा, उरई कालजी पुखारायां क्षेत्र के निवासियों को सीधे दिल्ली के लिए ट्रेन मिल जायेगी और मेरी मांग है कि पुखरायां स्टेशन जो उत्तर मध्य रेलवे के अंतर्गत आता है यहां पर दर्जनों चल रही गाड़ियों का ठहराव देने का कष्ट करें। 

श्री जय प्रकाश नारायण यादव (बाँका) : माननीय अध्यक्ष जी, मैं बजट पर बोलने के लिए खड़ा हुआ हूं। मैं अपनी बात एक दोहे से शुरु करता हूं:-

दोनों रहिमन एक से जौ लौं बोलत नाहि

जन परत है काक पिक ऋतु वसंत के माहि।

जब कौआ और कोयल गाछ पर वसंत ऋतु आने के बाद जब आवाज लगाते हैं तब सही पता चलता है। ऐसे पता नहीं चलता है कि यह कौआ बोल रहा है या कोयल बोल रही है। यहां पर बजट में कोयल की तरह कोई मिठास नहीं मिली। इस बजट में न गरीब के लिए, न दलित के लिए, न आदिवासियों के लिए, न पिछड़ों के लिए और न मॉइनोरिटी के लिए कुछ दिया गया है। बिहार को विशे­ा राज्य का दर्जा दिया जाए, यह सवाल हम हमेशा से उठाते रहे हैं। बिहार को 1 अरब 25 लाख करोड़ रुपये देने का जो विशे­ा पैकेज था, वह भी नहीं दिया गया है। पटना में एम्स बहुत पहले खुला, लेकिन अभी तक न वहां डॉक्टर हैं और न ही वहां पर सही इलाज की व्यवस्था है जिसको सभी स्वीकार करेंगे।

इसके साथ-साथ हम चाहते हैं कि बांका, भागलपुर, मुंगेर और जमुई में एम्स खुले। पर्यटन के लिए मंदार, सुल्तानगंज, अशोकधाम, लच्चौर, विक्रमशिला, भीमबांध, सीताकुंड, और ऋषिकुंड इत्यादि जगहों पर पर्यटन की व्यवस्था हो। नमामि गंगे योजना में सुल्तानगंज, भागलपुर, मुंगेर में बंदरगाह बने और वहां का रख-रखाव हो। एन.एच. के लिए हमने माननीय मंत्री जी से निवेदन किया कि लखीसराय के विद्यापीठ से, बांका से बरहट होकर के जिनहरा होते हुए चट्टी खिसार बांका तक एन.एच. की व्यवस्था हो, इसे उन्होंने स्वीकार भी किया। बिजली का प्रोजेक्ट 4000 मेगावॉट का बांका में लगना चाहिए जिसे राज्य सरकार ने मंजूरी दी है। केन्द्र सरकार ने पानी की व्यवस्था सुल्तानगंज से और कोल ब्लॉक के लिए पिरपैती से की है, मंजूरी के बाद अभी तक पड़ा हुआ है। पिछड़ा वर्ग आयोग बनना चाहिए। 

जहां तक रेल का सवाल है, रेल तो आम बजट में चला गया। रेल का खेल तो खत्म हो गया। आज रेलवे की स्थिति बहुत ही नाजुक है। एक समय में जब आदरणीय लालू जी देश के रेल मंत्री थे, उस समय रेलवे का किराया उन्होंने घटाया और मुनाफा बढ़ाया। लेकिन आज किराया बढ़ता जा रहा है और मुनाफा घटता जा रहा है। उन्होंने कहा था कि कोरीडोर बनाओ। माल ढ़ुलाई का अलग रखो और यात्री ढ़ुलाई का अलग रखो, लेकिन आज रेलवे की खस्ती हालत हो गई है। रेलवे बर्बाद हो गया है। 

सुल्तानगंज से होते हुए वेलहर-कटौरिया की तरफ जो रेल लाइन जाती है, वरियारपुर से होते हुए, बरहट होते हुए और लख्खीपुर होते हुए जो रेल लाइन मननपुर जाती है, उस रेल लाइन के लिए, भागलपुर में एक डी.आर.एम. कार्यालय के लिए बरसों से चर्चा हो रही है कि बन रहा है, लेकिन नहीं बन रहा है। बांका में वाशिंग पिट इंटरसिटी वहां से चले, स्टेशन का रख-रखाव हो, भागलपुर से राजधानी चले, सुल्तानगंज से गाड़ियां चलें। ...(व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : यह सब आप रेल बजट में बोलिए। अब आपकी बात पूरी हो गयी है। बैठिए।

श्री जय प्रकाश नारायण यादव: आदरणीय अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं केवल एक मिनट में अपनी बात समाप्त कर रहा हूं। मुंगेर में हमने कहा कि गुड्स यार्ड और वाशिंग पिट बने। आपने जितना समय दिया। इसके लिए मैं आपको धन्यवाद देता हूं।

श्रीमती विजया चक्रवर्ती (गुवाहाटी): मैडम, मैं आपकी बहुत आभारी हूं कि आपने मुझे बोलने का समय दिया है। जनरल बजट में विस्तार से हमारे ज्यादा लोग बोले। कभी कभी हम लोगों को ऐसा लगता है कि जैसे हल्दीघाटी के लिए कहते हैं कि राणा प्रताप पराजित हुए थे, ऐसी कहावत पर हम लोग सब विश्वास करते हैं, लेकिन अभी हिस्टोरीकल रिसर्च जो लोग करते हैं, उनका कहना है कि यह गलत है। हल्दीघाटी के युद्ध में राणा प्रताप जी जीत गये थे। पिछले 70 साल से जो लोग यह ध्रुव सत्य मानकर चलते थे, अब खुद ही वे लोग मानकर चलते हैं कि यह सब गलत है। 

जो सच मानता है, वह गलत हो जाता है, लेकिन कड़वा सच मानने में मन में थोड़ा संकोच होता है। वास्तव में हम लोगों ने देखा है कि भारत देश के जो जनसाधारण लोग हैं, जिन्होंने गरीब का नारा लगाया, गरीब के लिए सरकार, गांव के लिए सरकार और घर-घर में सरकार, यह सिर्फ नारा बन कर रह गया है, लेकिन किसी की उन्नति नहीं हुई है। प्रधानमंत्री जी आम लोगों को हर तरह की राहत देने और लोगों के कल्याण करने का विजन लेकर चलते हैं। नरेन्द्र मोदी जी स्ट्राँग डिसिजन लेने में कभी पीछे नहीं रहते हैं। 

यहां पर इलैक्शन की बात नहीं है। सामने इलैक्शन है, फिर भी कड़क डिसिजन लेने से नरेन्द्र मोदी जी कभी पीछे नहीं हटे हैं। हमने देखा है कि देश में काफी सुधार आया है, लेकिन कई लोग इसे मानने को तैयार नहीं हैं। हम लोग आम जनता के बीच में घूमते हैं, वे कहते हैं कि देश में सुधार आया है। जब बड़े-बड़े लोग बैंक में पैसा रखने के लिए रिक्वेस्ट करने जाते हैं तो हम लोगों के मन में संतो­ा होता है। हम लोगों के पास पैसा नहीं है, हम लोग खुश हैं, तुम लोग पैसे को जला रहे हो। यह बात ठीक है और सत्य को सत्य मानना जरूरी है। ...(व्यवधान) 

मेरे दादा-दादी दोनों स्वतंत्रता सेनानी थे। मैं दादी से पूछती थी कि आपको अंग्रेज साहब से डर नहीं लगता है। दादी ने कहा कि मुझे डर नहीं लगता। वे सूट-बूट पहनते हैं, अच्छी ड्रेस पहनते हैं, लेकिन उनसे बदबू आती है, शायद वे नहाते नहीं हैं। ऐसी बात नहीं है कि सूट-बूट पहनने से लोग अच्छे हो जाते हैं। जैसे व्यक्तिगत जीवन में स्वच्छता का प्रयोजन है, ऐसे ही आर्थिक जीवन में, राजनीतिक जीवन में और सामाजिक जीवन में स्वच्छता का प्रयोजन है। केवल सूट-बूट पहनने से ही सब कुछ नहीं हो जाता है। पिछली सरकार की स्वच्छता की कमी होने के कारण हर प्रकार की समस्या भारत में पैदा हुई है। नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने दोनों सदनों में इस संबंध में विस्तार से बातें कही हैं।...(व्यवधान)

महोदया, मैं असम की बात कहना चाहती हूं। ऐसा नहीं है कि 70 सालों से असम में काम नहीं हुआ है, लेकिन यह बात जरूर है कि अच्छा काम नहीं हुआ है। अभी असम में बीजेपी की सरकार है। आपको जानकर ताज्जुब होगा कि इन आठ महीनों में हर गांव में सड़क बनाना शुरू हो गया है। मोदी जी के इन्सप्रीशन से यह सरकार बनी है। यह सरकार अच्छा काम कर रही है और पिछली सरकार की ग्रामीण विकास की नीतियों के बारे में कहूंगी तो कुछ नहीं हुआ है।

माननीय अध्यक्ष : आप अपनी अच्छी बात कीजिए।

श्रीमती विजया चक्रवर्ती : असम की सबसे गंभीर समस्या घुसपैठ की समस्या है। कई माननीय सदस्यों ने इस बात को सदन में कल और आज उठाने की कोशिश की है। असम के पोरस बार्डर में जो देश के विभाजन के बाद, जो धर्म के आधार पर विभाजन हुआ फिर भी असम की पोरस बार्डर से घुसपैठ होती रहती है। वे लोग असम की जमीन पर चाहे फारेस्ट लैंड हो, रिवराइन लैंड हो, शंकर माधवदेव की धर्म सत्र की भूमि हो, या अभ्यारणय हो, वहां घुसपैठिए बैठ जाते हैं और पिछली सरकार के करप्ट अधिकारियों की सहायता से राशनकार्ड और वोटर लिस्ट में उनका नाम दर्ज करवा दिया जाता है।...(व्यवधान) वहां बांग्लादेश के दलाल हैं। वे दलाल यहां भी काम करते हैं और वहां भी काम करते हैं। यह असम की मुश्किल है। अभी तक असम में आधारकार्ड नहीं बना है क्योंकि उनकी वोटर लिस्ट में सुधारने की कोशिश जारी है, इसके लिए बहुत पैसे की जरूरत है। माननीय अरूण जी बैठे हैं, मैं उनसे निवेदन करती हूं कि इस काम में असम सरकार के लिए समुचित धनराशि का आबंटन करें। अभी स्कूल टीचर्स और छोटे-मोटे कर्मचारियों को वोटरलिस्ट के काम के लिए अप्वाइंटमेंट देते हैं। उसके लिए कुछ टेम्पररी पोस्ट्स की बहुत जरूरत है। 

मैं एक बात कह कर अपनी बात समाप्त करूंगी। असम में कई अनमैन्ड रेलवे क्रासिंग हैं। इसमें सुधार करना बहुत आवश्यक है। ब्रह्मपुत्र के ऊपर ब्रिज बनी है। रेलवे ब्रिज बनाने की बहुत जरूरी है और रेलवे में बहुत विभाग हैं, वहां लोगों की इम्प्लायमेंट हो सकती है। वहां पर लोकल इंप्लॉयमेंट बहुत जरूरी है।

SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL: Madam Speaker, the people of the country had a great expectation from this Budget. After demonetization, people thought that there may come some achche din (good days) through this Budget. That is what their feeling was. But after witnessing this Budget, they are all totally disappointed, especially the common people, poor workers, women and elderly people. All are unhappy with this Budget. 

Yesterday, the hon. Finance Minister told us that after demonetization there has not been much agitation among the people of the country. Even though it is not true, the people silently stood in queues because they had an aspiration that something will come in favor of them in the Budget. But now they are feeling that nothing has come out of it. 

Madam Speaker, I would like to ask the hon. Minister as to why the Government has not released the final statistics of how much money has arrived in banks. How much money has been unearthed after this decision? People thought that a large amount of money will be unearthed which will be used for the benefit of the poor people. But nothing is happening. 

I would also like to know from the hon. Finance Minister about the previous year’s Budget announcements and how much they have been fulfilled. I will highlight only one or two things. The day before yesterday, the hon. Prime Minister mentioned that the Government would save around Rs.22,000 crore in the Financial years of 2014-15 and 2015-16 because of launching of two-pronged approach on cooking gas subsidy – introducing direct bank transfers of the subsidy and asking better off consumers to voluntarily give up theirs. However, the CAG report on Implementation of PAHAL (DBTL) Pratyaksh Hanstantri Labh Yojan tabled in Parliament during the last Session rejects this claim. The audit has found that the saving from people voluntarily giving up LPG subsidy and direct bank transfers add up to less than Rs.2000 crore. It means that they would save only around Rs.2000 crore and not Rs.22,000 crore. The Audit has also found substantial systemic problems with the Direct Benefit Transfer in LPG scheme. So, that claim was actually bogus.

Then, let us take up Mudra scheme. The hon. Finance Minister has already clarified many times in this House that this scheme is for small and medium sectors. In my constituency I have attended many DLRC meetings. In the last meeting also I asked the bank officers as to how much money they have given for coir and fishing sectors which are traditional industries there. I can tell you, hon. Minister, that not a single person from these traditional industries of coir and fishing has got any benefit from this Mudra scheme. Actually, the figures shown by your officers are quite bogus and misleading. That is what I want to point out.

Then, I take up the biggest health sector announcement made in last year’s budget. The health protection scheme of Rs.1.3 lakh crore for providing health cover to the poor and the elderly is yet to be approved by the Cabinet. 

What about the Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana? You can ask any Member from the entire House as to how the project is going on. How can we do anything in a village without money? Nothing is happening. So, this is also a bogus project.

Then, what about the AMRUT scheme? My town has been selected under AMRUT scheme. But not a single work has been started in this scheme so far. I would like to ask from the hon. Finance Minister as to when the work is going to start there. So, these promises have not been fulfilled even after two years. 

Let me come to the health sector. There is only a marginal increase in the funding for health sector in the country. There are a lot of programmes which have been announced by the Central Government. The Government has announced that it has prepared an action plan to eliminate Kala-Azar, Filariasis, Leprosy, Measles and Tuberculosis. There is no roadmap to eliminate these diseases and sufficient money has also not been allocated. 

In respect of MGNREGS, there is an increase of Rs. 500 crore only. Last year, we spent Rs. 47,500 crore and this year, Rs. 48,000 crore have been allotted. There is a meagre enhancement. This will not meet the purpose of giving wages to the workers employed.

Regarding environment and forests, nothing has been given for climate change. There are a lot of activities due to which atmosphere is getting polluted. No major measure has been taken to control the pollution. There is no sufficient fund allocated in this area also.

Madam, the Budget also did not increase allocation towards achieving India’s commitment to renewable energy. 

The much talked about maternity benefit entitlement scheme of Rs. 6,000 per woman, announced by the. Prime Minister on December 31, 2016, has received a meagre allocation of Rs. 2,700 crore. As per the scheme details released by the Women and Child Development Ministry immediately after the Prime Minister’s announcement, State Governments will have to pool in 40 per cent of the amount with the assistance of the Centre. The conditional cash transfer is applicable only to women above the age of 19 years and up to two live children. The programme which was originally started by UPA-II Government in October, 2010 has so long been implemented on pilot basis in 53 districts. 

The Ministry officials said that the Budget Estimate of Rs. 2,700 crore has been drawn up taking into consideration 90 lakh beneficiaries annually. The latest available figure for live births, as per the Civil Registration System, 2013 of the Home Ministry, is 2.6 crore. As per the estimates of experts working in the area, a total of Rs. 16,000 crore is required for the scheme annually. This estimate also excludes women employed in the formal sector. The current allocation is truly based on a gross under-estimation and exclusions due to the two-child norm. In our country, women who have more than two children are largely poor people and marginalised people. It would be very unfortunate to exclude those who require this assistance the most. 

In Urban Development Ministry, the Government has slashed expenditure on some of the important schemes, like Crop Insurance Scheme and Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana. 

Another major thing is cut in allocation for the Urban Renewable Mission from Rs. 9,559 crore to Rs. 9,000 crore while urban population is increasing day by day. At the same time, the allocation of several Ministries is diminishing. 

Then, privatisation movement is also there. The Centre’s plan for disinvestment of public sector units’ shares to the tune of Rs. 72,500 crore shows that the Government is keen to dilute the State holdings and hand them over to corporate houses. 

In respect of primary education, there is no increase in allocation.

*SHRI D.K. SURESH (BANGALORE RURAL): I would like to say that the union budget presented by the Hon'ble Finance Minister is anti-poor, anti-farmer and anti-people budget. It has failed to meet the expectation of the 130 crore people of the country.

The budget comes at an important juncture when there has been a thrust by the government for a digitized and consequent cashless economy with the demonetization of high value currency notes undertaken in November last year. There was an air of expectation from the people of all strata of life, but this budget was a damp squib which did not meet anybody’s expectations.

Demonetization was touted as the biggest game changer when it was announced by the Prime Minister in Nov 2017. However, the budget did not give any account of the details of the effects of demonetization. It has given an account of how much high value currency was recovered and how much black money was unearthed. It is clear that demonetization has failed miserably and consequently, the effects of the failed demonetization effort reflect in the union budget of 2017-18. The Finance Minister has failed to give an account of the effects of demonetization in the said budget.

Demonetization created numerous problems for the Aam Admi. They suffered in silence expecting a big bang miracle, only to be made to accept a painful and unnecessary exercise which yielded absolutely no fruit. About 100 people died standing in queues during demonetization. Was this the intent of the Government? Has the Government given any compensation to the families of the people who died? Hundreds of thousands of jobs especially in the unorganized sector has been lost. The budget does not even take this into consideration as it is a sector that is unaccounted. What will happen to all the jobless people who worked on daily wages?

A number of claims have been made in the budget speech by the Finance Minister regarding longer term benefits of this move for the Indian Economy. Let me quote the hon'ble Finance Minister, “demonetization would lead the economy towards reduced corruption, greater digitization of the economy, increased flow of financial savings and greater formalization of the economy, all of which would eventually lead to higher GDP growth and tax revenues.” However, this view is not correct as the demonetization has induced an adverse effect on the economy in the medium term, especially for the groups that are in a weaker position.

Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji had attacked rural employment guarantee scheme MNREGS saying it served to fill the pocket of the Congress in an election rally. He also said “MGNREGA should stay as a proof of your failings. I will ensure MNREGA is never discontinued. After so many years in power, all you could do is to let a poor man dig ditches a few days a month.” Modi told the Opposition in February 2015.

This year, though the allocation under MGNREGA is made to Rs. 48,000 crore, it is not sufficient as the number of households seeking jobs under the scheme is increasing. Moreover, individual worker is not going to get more work or more pay and that is a big disappointment for landless farm workers.

I would like to point out that the budget exercise is a mere jugglery of words with regard to agriculture sector. Allocation of Rs. 10 lakh crore might be a phenomenal amount but when seen against the size of the farm economy and the fields of action involved, the allocation is just a pittance.

There has been too much talk on crop insurance but too little has been received by the farmers who have lost their crops, farmers are demanding the waiver of all crop loans sanctioned by nationalized banks. As per the available data, about farmers of the state availed about Rs. 29000 crores loan from Nationalized Banks. However, the Union Government has not taken any step to waive the farm loan availed by our poor farmers from the Nationalized Banks.

Increasing the allocation for crop loans from Rs. 9 lakh crores to 10 lakh crores will only keep farmers eternally debt ridden. However, on the ground, the number of big farmers who availed loan is higher than that of small and marginal farmers. It shows that banks are reluctant to give farm loan to the said section of the farmers. It is the reason why the living condition of poor farmers is gradually becoming worse. Hence, I request the Union Government to look into this and take necessary steps to provide farm loan to small and marginal farmers without subjecting them to hurdles.

With regard to MSP and Remunerative price, I would like to point out that there is no scientific and comprehensive mechanism put in place of fix Minimum Price and also no steps is announced for providing remunerative prices to farmers. Besides, there is no word about implementing the M.S. Swaminathan Commission recommendations on fixation of farm produce providing for 50% profit over and above the cost of production. I would like to ask the Hon'ble Finance Minister that in such a situation how the government would achieve its object of doubling farmers’ income without ensuring remunerative prices for farm produce? How can it would be ‘Achche Din’ for our farmers?

As far as farmers suicide is concerned, hundreds of our farmers committed suicides in Karnataka as well as other parts of the country due to shock over crop failure. The families of deceased farmers should be given adequate compensation to mitigate their agonies.

There is no special scheme or package announced to the state of Karnataka. The state of Karnataka needs a boost for as it has been affected by severe drought for more than a decade and facing difficulties due to factors like power-shortage, strikes, Cauvery riots and the impact of demonetization.

The Budget missed out on giving any additional income tax incentives to first-time home buyers or providing higher tax savings on housing loans and house insurance premiums. Nor did it raise house rent deduction limits. In the wake of demonetization and the huge money deposited in the banks, people were looking forward to an increase in income tax exemption limit. There were also multiple requests for the revision of tax slabs pertaining to senior citizens and super senior citizens (above 80 years). However, Hon'ble Finance Minister disappointed them.

In the Union budget, the Government has sought to incentivize greater use of non-cash transactions for small businesses by lowering the tax rate on presumptive income to 6% from 8% for all non-cash transactions. The Hon'ble Finance Minister also announced tax exemptions for manufacturers of point-of-sale (PoS) card reader, mobile PoS (mPOS), fingerprint readers and Iris scanners. I would like to point out that the government should have given full exemption in taxing to incentivize users to adopt non-cash transactions for small businesses instead of lowering it from 8% to 6%. The additional expenses involved in cashless transactions, like charges imposed on online transactions and withdrawals at ATMs, will be a huge burden on common man. This is an indication that the government doesn’t care over the pain and the difficulties undergone by the people during the demonetization period.

The Union Government has reduced the number of Schemes for Scheduled Castes from 294 to 256. In the year 2016-17, the total schemes for Scheduled Tribes were 307. It is brought down to only 261 in 2017-18. Only 11 new schemes for SCs and 8 new schemes for STs have been introduced in 2017-18.

As far as the allocation for children in this year’s budget is concerned, it sadly remained unchanged. It is a dismal 3.32% of the total Budget being allocated to children. I would like to point out that there is a need for a transformational change in the education system of the country. However the allocations for children have seen a meager increase to Rs. 71,305.35 crore this year from Rs. 65,758.45 crore in 2016-17 Budget.

There are 10,80,757 elementary schools in our country. The allocation for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, (SSA) in this year’s budget is up from Rs. 22,500 crore to Rs. 23,500 crore. If it is distributed with the number of elementary schools, each school get pittance.

For the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), Rs. 3830 crores are allocated, which is only Rs. 130 crore increase over last year. The RMSA has set out a target of ensuring universal access of secondary education by 2017 (gross enrolment rate, GER of 100%) and universal retention by 2020. But, according to the District Information System for Education (DISE) 2015-16, we are still struggling with 80% GER and 17% drop-out rate in secondary education. If these trends needs to change for secondary education, there has to be increased investment in the RMSA. For a country like ours, with the potential demographic dividend, it is imperative that the policy response and Budget outlay in the domain of public education need to be accorded higher priority. There is a very meager enhance for the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDM) from Rs. 9,700 crore in 2016-17 to Rs. 10,000 crore this year.

I would like to point out that the allocations under the SCSP, and the TSP in the 2017-18 budget is very inadequate to meet the demands of the communities. The SCSP comprises only 2.5% and the TSP only 1.53% of total allocations, which is not even the half of the mandated amount.

There has been a decrease in the allocation of Ministry of Social Justice and empowerment for equity and inclusion measures for SC and OBC kids, especially for education. Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) - Rs. 14,000 crore to Rs. 15,245 crore; and an increase of Rs. 339 crore (from Rs. 2,114.99 crore in 2016-17 to Rs. 2,454.42 crores).

The country is struggling to meet the targets of basic Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE), 2009. For instance, a number of schools do not have a boundary wall. Still most of the states do not adhere to the pupil-teacher ratio. On one hand, we have over a lakh single teacher schools in the country, and on the other hand, we still struggle with addressing quality teaching and learning at the school level.

Farmers expected some big announcements for the agriculture sector like thrust on improving irrigation infrastructure including inter-linking of rivers and enhancing water storage facilities. However, no such steps are taken by the Government in the budget.

The Indian MSME sector contributes about 45 per cent to manufacturing output and accounts for about 40 per cent of exports. The sector has vast potential to transform the business landscape of India. The MSME sector, which employs 106 million people, is taking major strides in staying competitive and making the most of the opportunities that will contribute to the growth of the country’s economy. However the union budget has nothing specific to revive the struggling MSME sector.

The Government had in September scrapped the 92-year old practice of presenting a separate railway budget and decided to present a combined general and railway budget for 2017-18 on 1 February 2017.

Major chunk of the allocations have been made to line doubling, including Hubballi-Vaso-da-Gama (Rs. 250 crore); Hotgi-Gadag (Rs. 138 crore); Hubballi-Chikkajajur (Bengaluru line) (Rs. 198 crore); Arsikere-Tumakuru (Rs. 138 crore) and Yelahanka-Penukonda (Rs. 120 crore) under South Western Railway (SWR).

Despite fervent demands to operationalize the new divisional office announced at Kalaburgi, only Rs. 1 lakh has been earmarked for creation of facilities under Solapur division of Central Railway. SWR got meager allocation (Rs. 3,146 crore) compared to neighbouring zones – Central Railway, Rs. 6419 crore; South Central Railway, Rs. 5,598 crore and Southern Railway, Rs. 5,785 crore.

I welcome the Third coaching terminal for Bengaluru, which would help to decongest Bengaluru city and Yeshwantpur terminals; the Ministry of Railways has allocated Rs. 32 crore for the third coaching terminal at Byappanahalli. The total cost of the terminal is Rs. 116 crore. The work is expected to be completed in three years. I would like to request the hon'ble Finance Minister to enhance the funds for the said terminal for its early completion.

I would like to draw the attention of the Government towards the need of allocation for the Railway line between Bengalore and Satyamangala via Kanakapura and Malavalli. The said railway line was announced about one and a half decade ago. Previously, Railway budgets were allocated for the survey of the railway line. However, there is no mention in this year budget about the Bangalore and Styamangala via Kanakapura and Malavalli railway line. Therefore, I urge upon the Government to allocate sufficient fund for the said project as this railway would help the economic development of backward regions of Ramnagara, Mandya and Chamarajanagar districts of the state of Karnataka.

I would also like to urge upon the Union Government to allocate funds for Bengaluru Suburban Rail. The Centre had promised to take up the projects with the State Government sharing 80 per cent of the cost. But the state had requested for a 50:50 formula. Suburban rail needs Rs. 100 crore, but nothing has been allotted for it. I would like to draw the attention of the Government that the state of Karnataka has been facing severe infrastructural crisis in Bengaluru city. Considering the fact that the state of Karnataka is facing frequent droughts and suffering financial loss due to crop failure and drought relief activities, the Government of India should come forward to cost sharing 50:50 for the Suburban rail project in Bengaluru.

With regard to ROB and RUBs, I would like to mention that the Government has sanctioned only one Rail Under Bridge (RUB) in the budget. Whereas there is a need of 50 Rail Under Bridges. Electrification of trunk routes, Bengaluru to Hosur and Yeshwanthpur to Tumakuru line, has been sanctioned without funds. The Union Government wants all projects to completely rely on institutional funding, that is, loans from private groups. However, I am of the opinion that hon'ble Finance Minister should have allocated funds to begin the works of the RUBs.

I would also like to mention that a meager Rs. 40 crore has been allotted for passenger amenities for the entire state, while Tamil Nadu has got Rs. 80 crore, and Andhra Pradesh Rs. 100 crore. It is really a disappointing towards the people of Karnataka. The Union Government has done injustice to allocate funds for the railway projects in Karnataka.

Bangalore’s main railway station needs to be decongested. A project has been proposed to decongest the Krantiveera Sangolli Rayanna station by acquiring 3 acres of land in Binny Mill. But, the hon'ble Finance Minister has not allocated any funds for the said proposal. I request that the Government look into this and help decongest the railway station for smooth travel of passengers.

Overall, this budget has fallen far short of expectations of the common man. It fails to address the realities of the common man and ignores his requirements in order to enable him to enjoy “Acchhe Din”. The NDA Government has failed to deliver on all of its promises and is fooling the people of this country over and over again with cleverly worded speeches with no substance and little actual work on the ground.

Before concluding, in this speech, the hon. Finance Minister has mentioned Gandhiji’s name four times. He remembered Gandhiji and that is a very good thing. When do you remember someone who is great, who can give us benefit, who can give us ashirwad? We remember them when we are in trouble. We also run to the temple when we are in trouble. ये तो कहा जाता है कि ईश्वर कण-कण में है, लेकिन फिर भी हम मन्दिर जाते हैं। इसका उत्तर एक साधु ने बहुत ही अच्छे ढ़ँग से दिया था। ईश्वर तो कण-कण में है फिर हम मन्दिर क्यों जाते हैं, इसका उत्तर देते हुए साधु ने कहा कि हवा तो चारों ओर है, पर जो हवा आम के पेड़ के नीचे बैठकर हम महसूस करते हैं, वह हवा कुछ अलग है। 

In this Budget the Finance Minister quoted the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, saying, ‘A right cause never fails’. He also said later while speaking about the Government’s intent to celebrate the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi in 2019, that the Government will take all steps to celebrate it in a befitting manner. I am reminded of this because at that time while writing my editorial I was a bit critical saying how a newly formed Bharatiya Janata Party, which broke away from the Janata Party in the 80s could do this. After that defeat when the Janata Party and all of us were projecting Babu Jagjivan Ram as the Prime Ministerial candidate, we failed and Mrs. Gandhi came back to power. … (Interruptions) At that time Bharatiya Janata Party was the name. Advaniji is here. When Bharatiya Janata Party was formed, a word was coined by both Advaniji and Atalji and that word is ‘Gandhian Socialism’. I was trying to go through Gandhian economy. … (Interruptions) It is Bharatiya Janata Party.

The Finance Minister remembered Gandhiji. That is a very good thing. Remember Gandhiji, his economic policy, and Gandhian socialism which was propagated in the 80s. Of course in 1984 only two Members got elected. But that is a cause which this party should fight for. Do not go in for consumerism to a great extent saying that by producing more we can create more demand. We will develop our indigenous market but not merely by producing more. What was Gandhiji’s idea? Produce by the masses so that consumption can take place, and not production for the masses by a few. That was the economy he had said. What I said earlier about putting more money in the hands of consumers, I was very much aware and I was quoting Gandhian economy. It is not contradictory, it is more supplementary in the sense that we have to have more money in the hands of our people. I am not dealing with the aspect of plastic money or cash. But it is something that is important. 

They were talking about Charvaka and Chanakya. But the idea here is, why cannot we have an economy in our country where we can create a market of our own instead of depending on others? That should be our approach. Ultimately what Gandhiji had said, Madam, is that it is the happiness that has to come. Whatever work we do in this House or outside being in the Government, it is the happiness of the people that is important. That is what Gandhiji had repeatedly spoken about. That is what Gandhian socialism actually portrayed in the 80s. Please remember that. Please remember that and work for that so that people will be happy.

Thank you.

*SHRI K. ASHOK KUMAR (KRISHNAGIRI): I express my hearty gratitude and indebtedness to our beloved immortal Leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA, before I express my views on the General Budget 2017-18.

The Union Budget 2017-18 has been presented at a very crucial moment especially after the Demonetization episode. This Budget represents a significant forward movement from the previous Budgets presented by the Finance Minister.

The emphasis on agriculture and enhancing farmer’s income are welcome features of the Budget. While the Union Finance Minister spoke about the general revival of growth in the agricultural sector this year, he did not highlight the acute drought situation which has affected agriculture in the southern part of the country, in particular Tamil Nadu. A special package for drought affected farmers would have been a very welcome feature of the Budget.

In the area of Education, while we welcome initiatives like the Innovation Fund for Secondary Education which would give greater flexibility to State Governments to pursue strategies and implement schemes which are suitable and appropriate to local conditions, we are seriously concerned about the implications of proposals relating to the National Testing Agency to conduct nationwide entrance examinations.

In the Health sector, we welcome the proposal to create an additional 5000 PG seats and to strengthen Health Sub Centres. However, we are skeptical about the proposal for structural transformation of Medical Education. The draft Medical Council Bill proposed by the NITI Aayog has a number of problematic features which diminish the powers of State Governments and also discriminate against a State like Tamil Nadu which is relatively advanced in medical education. Hence, I urge the Union Government to take up any such reforms only after adequate consultation with the State Governments and all stake holders.

We welcome the announcements relating to the affordable housing sector. The proposed reforms in the Labour codes should not compromise the existing rights and entitlements of the workers. We welcome the enhanced allocation for Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Minorities. With the substantial enhancement of funds for Scheduled Caste welfare, the long pending arrears for the Post Matric Scholarship scheme for States like Tamil Nadu would be released immediately.

We welcome the announcement of the Rail Raksha Kosh (the Railway Safety Fund) with a substantial allocation of Rs. 1 lakh crore. In particular, the elimination of all unmanned level crossings and broad gauge by 2020 is a very timely measure.

Metropolitan Chennai has been growing rapidly and traffic volumes have increased greatly. To promote and ease public transport of various forms including metro rail and to ensure that the share of public transportation in Chennai city is substantially increased was accorded top most priority by our beloved Leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA, during her golden reign.

Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA was instrumental and played a stellar role in implementing the Chennai Metro Rail Project Phase I. The Chennai Metro Rail Project Phase II has been included in the Rolling Plan for the current year for Japan International Co-operation Agency (JICA) for funding. A Detailed Feasibility Report for the expansion of the Chennai Metro Rail Project along 3 corridors – North West to South East; West to East; and an orbital corridor at an estimated cost of Rs. 44,000 crores has already been approved by the Government of Tamil Nadu.

I urge upon the Government to support the proposed Phase II of the Metro Rail Project of Chennai and to ensure that all necessary clearances are provided expeditiously to fulfill the dream of our visionary Leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA to provide fillip to the public transport system in the Chennai Metropolitan city.

The extremely heavy rains during the North East Monsoon in December 2015 have caused enormous devastation to standing crops, property and public infrastructure besides loss of livelihood, loss of life and cattle. The floods in Tamil Nadu were declared as a “Calamity of Severe Nature”. The Hon'ble former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA had requested the Hon'ble Prime Minister to kindly consider her two memoranda for assistance on account of flood damages and devastation and release the necessary funds at the earliest to meet the State Government’s requirement of Rs. 25,912.45 crores. But even a year after the central team had inspected and given its report on the devastations caused by the heavy rains and cyclone in December 2015, the Union Government has so far not provided adequate relief to Tamil Nadu for relief and restoration efforts due to the rain and flood damage.

In December 2016, Cyclone Vardah had caused severe damages to the coastal regions of Northern Tamil Nadu, particularly in Chennai City and adjoining districts of Tiruvallur, Kanchipuram and Cuddalore uprooting several thousands of trees and electric lamp posts besides damaging the roads and other infrastructures of the people. The Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu met the Hon'ble Prime Minister and submitted a 142-page memorandum seeking an assistance of Rs. 22,573 crores from the Central Government to undertake reconstruction works in areas affected by cyclone Vardah and reiterated the demand for an ‘on account’ grant of Rs. 1,000 crore for immediate requirements.

I urge the Union Government to consider in this budget the genuine demands of the Government of Tamil Nadu to immediately release an adequate relief grant to Tamil Nadu for being devastated by two back to back calamities of severe nature.

Our beloved immortal leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA had consistently urged the Union Government for the interlinking of peninsular rivers and for the nationalization of rivers to facilitate economic development in the country. The Government has notified the special committee for interlinking of rivers, as requested by our Leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA. All inter-State rivers should be nationalized so that water resources of the country are optimally utilized.

The River Cauvery is the lifeline of Tamil Nadu, particularly the millions of farmers in the delta regions in Tamil Nadu. With the notification of the final order of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, the scheme for Modernization of the canal System in the Cauvery Basin at a cost of Rs. 11,421 crore may be accorded approval. This request of our beloved leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA may be approved at the earliest.

The Tamil Nadu Government had submitted the proposal to the Central Water Commission for the extension, renovation and modernization of Grand Anicut Canal in Thanjavur and Pudukkottai districts at the cost of Rs. 2,610 crore. The Commission also gave the in-principle consent. I urge the Government to consider this important proposal and allocate the requested funds for the implementation of Grand Anicut project.

The Government of Tamil Nadu had sought the assistance of the Union Government for implementation of the proposal to divert the flood waters of Cauvery to drought prone areas by linking the Rivers Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar at a cost of Rs. 5166 crores. This project proposal should be approved expeditiously. Like-wise, the Athikadavu-Avinashi Flood Canal Scheme at an estimated cost of Rs. 1862 Crores may also be sanctioned on a priority basis.

Sensing the importance of cleaning, restoration and conservation of rivers, our visionary immortal leader Puratchithalaivi AMMA had announced Tamil Nadu Vision-2023, a far-sighted, Multi-Disciplinary Mission, giving utmost importance to create and achieve a clean, pollution free environment. The document – includes profiles of 217 infrastructure projects in six major sectors – energy, transport, industrial and commercial infrastructure, urban infrastructure and services, agriculture and human development which sets target of Rs. 15 lakh crore investments.

The Dream, Vision and Mission of our immortal leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA, many far-sighted projects envisaged in Tamil Nadu Vision-2023 and lots of efforts have already been taken under Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust (CRRT) to reduce the sewage let into the rivers and other water bodies of Chennai mega city.

Apart from the Adayar River Eco-Restoration Project, Rs. 150 crore was allocated out of the Environment Protection and Renewable Energy Fund to restore lake, water bodies in Chennai and other Cities, including Rs. 42 crore for restoration of Chetpet Lake. A major initiative will be undertaken during the coming financial year by launching the Coovum River Restoration Project to be implemented at a total cost of Rs. 3,833.62 crore in 5 years with Chennai River Restoration Trust as the nodal agency.

The major projects in pipeline are, creation and restoration of water bodies in Chennai and adjoining areas at the cost of Rs. 500 crores and restoration of Chennai Waterways at the cost of Rs. 10000 crores, the remediation/closure of Perungudi/ Kodungaiyur dump yards at a cost of Rs. 150 crores and Greenfield Regional Landfill and Waste Processing Facility at the cost of Rs. 150 crores and an Integrated Waste Collection and Transfer at a cost of Rs. 200 crores. Further, there are 100% sanitized and open defecation free city project at the cost of Rs. 300 crores and slum-free city program at the cost of Rs. 25000 crores, which include 100% sewerage coverage program at the cost of Rs. 7000 crores.

Last year an allocation of Rs. 100 crore each for celebrating the Birth Centenary of Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay and the 350th Birth Anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh was made. In the same way, Rs. 200 crores should be allocated for Tamil Nadu State for celebrating the Birth Centenary (1917-2017) of “Bharat Ratna” Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G. Ramachandran, founder of AIADMK Party and Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for three consecutive terms from 1977 to 1987.

Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA had played key role in launching and implementing the free laptop scheme for school and college students studying in Government and Government Aided institutions. It was intended as an effort to bridge the digital divide, which the Government of India has also now recognized. The introduction of new Digital Literacy Mission Scheme for rural India to cover around 6 crore additional household within the next 3 years is good for the rural people. The Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadi Yojana is similar to the Amma Marunthagam Scheme launched by the Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA.

The Union Government has included all ingredients required for the popular Budget. The responsibility of implementing the schemes and projects envisaged within the stipulated time is with the Union Government and we hope the Union Government would address the requirements of people in various States without derailing the federal system and the democratic principles provided by the constitution of India.

*DR. J. JAYAVARDHAN (CHENNAI SOUTH): On behalf of our Party, AIADMK, which is following the policies and principles adopted by late revered leader, Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, I would like to put forth the following views for the consideration of the Union Finance Minister and also the hon. Prime Minister. I am happy to note that the Union Finance Minister has heeded to the repeated calls of our late hon. Chief Minister Amma, who had strongly advocated the idea of doing away with the artificial and irrelevant distinction between Plan and Non-Plan schemes in the Budget. I would like to emphasis on several sectors in which immediate action of the Union Government is required with regards to Tamil Nadu.

With regard to agriculture sector, to give a boost to usage of non-conventional energy with regards to use of Solar Power in Agriculture and to take up the programme on a large scale for catering to the demand for the farmers, it is necessary that GOI should consider enhancing the share of Government of India to 80% under Ministry of New and Renewable Energy funds and the remaining 20% can be met by the State and the farmers.

In Tamil Nadu, the National Horticulture Mission is implemented in cluster approach with the prime objective of achieving holistic growth of Horticulture in the State. There are seven varied agro climatic zones existing in the State which support cultivation of wide variety of Horticultural crops. At present, the National Horticulture Mission is being implemented only in 22 districts. It is requested that the implementation of the NHM may be extended to the remaining 9 districts also to extend the scheme benefits to the farming community of the entire State so as to 
 reap the benefit of agro-climatic conditions and to improve livelihood status of our farmers. As for Micro Irrigation Scheme in Tamil Nadu, it is requested to allocate more funds to Tamil Nadu for micro irrigation so as to cover the entire irrigable area as envisaged under the Vision Tamil Nadu 2023. With regard to allocation under Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) to Tamil Nadu, the allocation for Tamil Nadu under RKVY for the year 2016-17 may be restored to at least the initially indicated interim allocation of Rs. 509.55 crores. With regard to establishing APEDA in Tamil Nadu, give the States production and export potential, the availability of four international airports and four major seaports and connectivity within the State, the establishment of a full- fledged Regional Office of APEDA in Tamil Nadu would greatly facilitate exports and further encourage the growers and exporters of the State. Our revered leader Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had already made this request in June, 2016. Considering the importance of APEDA office in Tamil Nadu, I reiterate this demand and request for an early decision in this regard.

For rural development, thousands of families in Tiruvallur and Kancheepuram districts have lost their houses and livelihood due to the devastation caused by the “Vardah Cyclone”. The people living in kutcha, semi-pucca houses and houseless rural poor people are the most affected and hence it is very essential to construct disaster resistant houses for the affected households in Kancheepuram and Tiruvallur districts. Hence, it is requested to sanction at least 10,000 additional new houses to rural areas of both Tiruvallur and Kancheepuram districts under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Grameen) (PMAY(G)) Scheme as a special case, in addition to the 1.31 lakh houses already allotted for 2016-17 to Tamil Nadu. With regard to Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, under the MGNREGS, there is a pendency in the committed wage liability of Rs. 794 crores. This leads to delay in payment of wages and puts the workers to a lot of hardship, especially women, because 85% of MGNREGS beneficiaries are women. There is already a committed wage liability of Rs. 794 crores pending for 2 months. Further, Rs. 1200 crores (Rs. 600 crores under wage component and Rs. 600 crores from material component) is required for the remaining period of 2016-17. We request Government of India to release Rs. 1994 crores for urban development. The Detailed Project Report for the 134 km Chennai Peripheral Ring Road (CPRR) connecting Ennore Port in the north through the Northern Port Access Road, to Mamallapuram in the south on the East coast Road (ECR) to provide better connectivity and for decongesting Chennai city has been prepared. The CPRR Project has been proposed for external funding from the Japanese International Cooperation Agency (JICA) through the Government of India at a total cost of Rs. 12,301 crores including Rs. 921 crores for establishing an Intelligent Transport System (ITS) in Chennai. JICA is also very keen to support this project. I request that this project may be fast tracked and JICA financing secured at the earliest as it would help in improving the traffic conditions in the city and result in better port connectivity with regard to Chennai Urban Infrastructure Project. The Chennai Urban Infrastructure Project aims at upgradation of roads and bridges and construction of grade separators in Chennai at a total project cost of Rs. 5788 crores. This project consists of two components to be executed by the Corporation of Chennai and by the Highways Department. A Detailed Project Report (DPR) is under preparation and the project may be considered for inclusion in the JICA Rolling Plan for 2016-17.

As far as school education is concerned, the 13th Finance Commission grant of Rs. 164 crores for 2014-15 was withheld by Government of India on the ground that requisite growth in expenditure was not shown by the State Governments. The fact that the growth in expenditure was not achieved because of shortfall in fund release under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan to Tamil Nadu by Government of India in 2012-13 has been completely overlooked. The State has thus been wrongfully penalized for short release of funds by Government of India. Hence, the grant of Rs.164 crores sanctioned by 13th Finance Commission must be released to Tamil Nadu. With regard to release of Grants under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, even though the State Government has submitted all necessary documentation, the funds for the years 2015-16 and 2016-17 for a total amount of Rs. 1378.56 crores are yet to be released by Union Government.

With regard to Information and Technology, the Government of Tamil Nadu under the leadership of the late Hon'ble Chief Minister, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had revived the “Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV” (TACTV) Corporation in order to provide Cable TV services at an affordable cost to the public. TACTV submitted its applications for grant of Digital Addressable System (DAS) License to GOI on 5.7.2012 and 23.11.2012. These applications are still pending with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The deliberate non-issuance of DAS license to the State Government owned Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation by the previous UPA Government was only to facilitate particular private business interests. Since then, several representations and letters have been sent to Government of India but the license is yet to be issued even though more than two years have elapsed since the present NDA Government took over. It is requested to expedite the issue of DAS license to TACTV.

With regard to Chennai Metro Rail Project Phase II, Metropolitan Chennai has been growing rapidly and traffic volumes have increased greatly. It was the goal of our Revered Leader the late Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma to promote public transport of various forms including metro rail to ensure that the share of public transportation in Chennai city is substantially increased. Phase I of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, which is currently under implementation, will cover the total length of 45 km. The Phase I extension from Washermenpet to Tiruvotriyur/WIMCO Nagar covering further 9.51 kms at a cost of Rs.3,770 crores has been recently approved by the Government of India and the work inaugurated by our Revered Leader Puratchi Thalaivi Amma. There is a need to substantially expand the metro rail network in the city of Chennai. A detailed feasibility report for the expansion of the Chennai Metro Rail Project along three corridors at an estimated cost of Rs. 44,000 crore has been approved by the Government of Tamil Nadu. It has also been included in the rolling plan of Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for funding. Our Revered Leader, late Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had requested the Hon'ble Prime Minister to instruct the Ministry of Urban Development and Ministry of Finance to support the proposed Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project so that the work can commence early. The Detailed Project Report (DPR) for Phase II being prepared by M/s RITES will be ready by the end of December 2016. As the inauguration of passenger services on the second elevated section from the Airport to Little Mount Stations was the last public engagement in which our Revered Leader the late Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had participated in on September 21, 2016, it would be most fitting if Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project is given early approval by the Government of India.

As far as amendment to the Memorandum of Understanding is concerned, the Chennai Metro Rail Project is being implemented on a joint ownership basis between the Government of India and Government of Tamil Nadu. In the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) that was entered into between Government of India, Government of Tamil Nadu and Chennai Metro Rail Limited, for implementing the project, the then UPA Government and the then DMK led State Government had included certain clauses which are not in the interest of the State Government and of the Project. These clauses do not provide for an equitable sharing of risks and costs. Our revered Leader Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had sought amendments to certain clauses of MOU, in particular, treating the land cost as the equity contribution of the Central or State Government who are transferring the land; sharing of any escalation in project cost and foreign exchange fluctuation beyond the approved project completion period equally by the two Governments; and sharing of both operational losses and profits between the Government of India and the State Government. In response to the Memorandum submitted by our Revered Leader Puratchi Thalaivi Amma on 14th June, 2016, the Ministry of Urban Development indicated that the issue need not be perused further as 80 percent of project work has been completed. However, the Ministry of Urban Development has persisted with the same clauses and made them even more stringent in the draft MOU they have shared for the Chennai Metro Rail Phase I Extension. The Government of Tamil Nadu has taken up the issue again it is requested that the Ministry of Urban Development should consider this issue with an open mind and in the spirit of co-operative federalism so that the legitimate concerns of the State Government regarding the MOU are adequately addressed.

With regard to Railways lands taken by Chennai Metro Rail Limited on lease basis, I would like to mention that Chennai Metro Rail Limited has taken the Railway lands on long lease basis for the implementation of the Chennai Metro Rail Project on payment of 99% of the market value for the period of 35 years and extendable for another 35 years. In spite of the payment of 99% of the land value, the surface rights have been retained by Railways which is unfair. A policy view has to be taken by Government of India to transfer Railway lands to Metro Rail Project on permanent basis on collection of 100% of the land value as is being done in respect of lands transferred from other Central Government Departments/ Agencies with full rights or if full rights cannot be given for justifiable reasons by Railways, then only nominal/token amount shall be charged for restricted rights. Further, no collection of charges should be made for underground tunneling work done by Metro Rail Administration below the Railway land. A nominal fee as track rent may be charged on crossing of Railway track alone. This issue requires a speedy resolution.

With regard to establishment of Special Purpose Vehicle for execution of Railway Projects, the Ministry of Railways has circulated a draft Joint Venture Agreement to be entered into between the Ministry of Railways and the Government of Tamil Nadu to form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to execute Railway Projects in Tamil Nadu. Our Revered Leader, late Hon'ble Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had indicated that the Government of Tamil Nadu was in principle willing to participate in establishing a SPV with the Ministry of Railways. She had requested that the draft MOU required revisions in order to evolve a fair, balanced and acceptable agreement. The manner in which the draft Joint Venture Agreement is worded leaves us with a distinct impression that the State Governments are being roped in to bear the cost burden on what is essentially a Union Government responsibility under the Constitution. Further, the State Government will be required to bear the losses, if any, while the Railways retain preferential terms for themselves in the area of project approvals, revenue realization, asset ownership and asset handover. Tamil Nadu has certain concerns regarding certain clauses of the draft Joint Venture Agreement which has been circulated by the Ministry of Railways, which include the following: Even though it is termed as Joint venture Agreement, the Agreement is in the nature of Shareholders agreement. Ideally there should be two separate Agreements a (i) JV Agreement between State Government and Ministry of Railways; and (ii) Shareholders Agreement amongst State Government, Ministry of Railways and other Shareholders. This is necessary in order to make a distinction between JV Partners and other Shareholders. The JV Agreement should clarify the roles and responsibilities, rights and powers of State Government and Ministry of Railways as JV Partners, while the rights and responsibilities of Shareholders are substantially driven by the provisions of Companies Act and other commercial understanding between the Shareholders. In Clause 2.1, the Scope of the JV does not clearly mention about the Design responsibility. The responsibility for preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR), including detailed design may be taken by the Railways through one of their agencies like RITES and the cost of preparing the DPR, at a pre-agreed level may be treated as equity contribution by Railways in the JV. Further, as the Railway Design Approval process is very laborious and time consuming, the Railways must commit in the JV Agreement that they will take the responsibility for expeditious Design Approval at no additional cost to the JV. Under Clause 2.2(a) and 2.6, the paid up equity base of the JV should be kept to the minimum, and the balance funding for actual project finance should be brought in by the shareholders in the form of Optional Convertible Preference Shares/Optional Convertible Debentures. This will avoid the necessity for the shareholders to invest huge sums in the beginning and funds can be mobilized from the shareholders as and when required for investment in subsidiaries. This would be a more efficient use of capital of funds. Under Clause 2.3 the territorial scope of JV has been described as territory of India. While this is acceptable, it should be made clear that activities would be limited to the State and where beyond the State, then for the benefit of the State.
